crises.note: Cross-cutting indicators that may be relevant for this disaster (not specific to it).

indicators.name: Human Development Index
indicators.description: The Human Development Index (HDI) measure development by combining indicators of life expectancy, educational attainment and income into a composite index.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Poverty & Development

indicators.name: Multidimensional Poverty Index
indicators.description: The Multidimensional Poverty (MPI) Index identifies overlapping deprivations at the household level across the same three dimensions as the Human Development Index (living standards, health, and education) and shows the average number of poor people and deprivations with which poor households contend.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Poverty & Development

indicators.name: Gender Inequality Index
indicators.description: The Gender Inequality Index (GII) reflects gender-based disadvantages in three dimensions—reproductive health, empowerment and the labour market. The value of GII range between 0 to 1, with 0 being 0% inequality, indicating women fare equally in comparison to men and 1 being 100% inequality, indicating women fare poorly in comparison to men.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Inequality

indicators.name: Income Gini coefficient - Inequality in income or consumption
indicators.description: Gini index measures the extent to which the distribution of income or consumption expenditure among individuals or households within an economy deviates from a perfectly equal distribution. Thus a Gini index of 0 represents perfect equality, while an index of 100 implies perfect inequality.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Inequality

indicators.name: Humanitarian aid per capita
indicators.description: The Financial Tracking Service (FTS) is a centralized source of curated, continuously updated data and information on humanitarian funding flows, where government donors, UN-administered funds, UN agencies, NGOs and other humanitarian actors exchange data and information. The indicator is expressed as the three-year rolling sum of total humanitarian assistance received divided by population (USD per capita), with the three-year aggregation used to smooth single-year emergency spikes and better reflect the structural humanitarian funding base of a country.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economical Dependency

indicators.name: Humanitarian aid per capita instability
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in humanitarian aid funding caused by external shocks and donor behaviour. Unstable humanitarian funding has a large effect on the planning and delivery of emergency response and increases the risk of unmet needs in crisis-affected populations. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the value of annual humanitarian aid per capita and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of humanitarian aid per capita) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Development aid per capita
indicators.description: Net Official Development Assistance (ODA) consists of disbursements of concessional loans and grants by official agencies of the Development Assistance Committee (DAC), multilateral institutions, and non-DAC countries to promote economic development and welfare in ODA recipient countries. The indicator is expressed as the two-year lagged sum of annual net ODA received divided by population (USD per capita), with the two-year aggregation accounting for disbursement lags between aid commitments and actual delivery.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Development aid per capita instability
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in the absolute volume of official development assistance per person caused by external shocks and changes in donor allocations. Unstable per capita ODA has a large effect on the availability of resources for basic services and infrastructure investment and increases the risk of development reversals in fragile and aid-dependent states. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the annual value of net ODA received per capita and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of ODA per capita) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Net ODA received (% of GNI)
indicators.description: Net Official Development Assistance (ODA) consists of disbursements of loans made on concessional terms (net of repayments of principal) and grants by official agencies of the members of the Development Assistance Committee (DAC), by multilateral institutions, and by non-DAC countries to promote economic development and welfare in countries and territories in the DAC list of ODA recipients. It includes loans with a grant element of at least 25 percent (calculated at a rate of discount of 10 percent).
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Net ODA received instability (% of GNI)
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in official development assistance relative to its national income caused by external shocks and changes in donor priorities. Unstable ODA as a share of GNI has a large effect on public revenues and long-term development planning and increases fiscal risk for aid-dependent economies. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the annual value of net ODA received as a percentage of GNI and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of ODA % GNI) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Volume of remittances as a proportion of total GDP (%)
indicators.description: Personal remittances received as proportion of GDP is the inflow of personal remittances expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Volume of remittances as a proportion of total GDP instability (%)
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in personal remittances relative to its economy caused by external shocks including economic downturns in host countries, exchange rate movements, and changes in migration policy. Unstable remittance inflows have a large effect on household income, private consumption, and poverty levels and increase the vulnerability of remittance-dependent populations to sudden income loss. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the annual value of personal remittances received as a percentage of GDP and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of remittances % GDP) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Government effectiveness
indicators.description: The Government effectiveness captures perceptions of the quality of public services, the quality of the civil service and the degree of its independence from political pressures, the quality of policy formulation and implementation, and the credibility of the government's commitment to such policies.
indicators.inform_group: Lack of Coping Capacity > Institutional > Governance

indicators.name: Corruption Perception Index
indicators.description: The CPI scores and ranks countries based on how corrupt a country’s public sector is perceived to be. It is a composite index, a combination of surveys and assessments of corruption, collected by a variety of reputable institutions.
indicators.inform_group: Lack of Coping Capacity > Institutional > Governance

indicators.name: Sendai Framework Monitor indicator E-1
indicators.description: The indicator for the Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) activity in the country comes from the score of adoption and implementation of national DRR strategies in line with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030 (Sendai target E1 and SDG indicator 13.1.2). Sendai framework indicators measure progress in achieving the global targets of the Sendai Framework, and determine global trends in the reduction of risk and losses.
indicators.inform_group: Lack of Coping Capacity > Institutional > DRR implementation

indicators.name: Reporting frequecncy of Sendai Framework Monitor indicator E-1 in last 10 years
indicators.description: The indicator for the Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) activity in the country comes from the score of adoption and implementation of national DRR strategies in line with the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015-2030 (Sendai target E1 and SDG indicator 13.1.2). Sendai framework indicators measure progress in achieving the global targets of the Sendai Framework, and determine global trends in the reduction of risk and losses.
indicators.inform_group: Lack of Coping Capacity > Institutional > DRR implementation

indicators.name: Adult literacy rate
indicators.description: Total is the percentage of the population age 15 and above who can, with understanding, read and write a short, simple statement on their everyday life.
indicators.inform_group: Lack of Coping Capacity > Infrastructure > Communication

indicators.name: Access to electricity
indicators.description: Access to electricity is the percentage of population with access to electricity. Electrification data are collected from industry, national surveys and international sources.
indicators.inform_group: Lack of Coping Capacity > Infrastructure > Communication

indicators.name: Internet Users
indicators.description: Internet users are individuals who have used the Internet (from any location) in the last 3 months.
indicators.inform_group: Lack of Coping Capacity > Infrastructure > Communication

indicators.name: Mobile celluar subscriptions
indicators.description: Mobile cellular telephone subscriptions are subscriptions to a public mobile telephone service using cellular technology, which provide access to the public switched telephone network. Post-paid and prepaid subscriptions are included.
indicators.inform_group: Lack of Coping Capacity > Infrastructure > Communication

indicators.name: Improved sanitation facilities
indicators.description: Access to improved sanitation facilities refers to the percentage of the population using improved sanitation facilities. The improved sanitation facilities include flush/pour flush (to piped sewer system, septic tank, pit latrine), ventilated improved pit (VIP) latrine, pit latrine with slab, and composting toilet.
indicators.inform_group: Lack of Coping Capacity > Infrastructure > Physical Connectivity

indicators.name: Improved water source
indicators.description:
The indicator defines the percentage of population with reasonable access (within one km) to an adequate amount of water (20 litres per person) through a household connection, public standpipe well or spring, or rain water system.
An improved drinking-water source is defined as one that, by nature of its construction or through active intervention, is protected from outside contamination, in particular from contamination with faecal matter.
indicators.inform_group: Lack of Coping Capacity > Infrastructure > Physical Connectivity

indicators.name: People using at least basic sanitation services (% of population)
indicators.description: The percentage of people using at least basic sanitation services, that is, improved sanitation facilities that are not shared with other households.  This indicator encompasses both people using basic sanitation services as well as those using safely managed sanitation services.   Improved sanitation facilities include flush/pour flush to piped sewer systems, septic tanks or pit latrines; ventilated improved pit latrines, compositing toilets or pit latrines with slabs.
indicators.inform_group: Lack of Coping Capacity > Infrastructure > Physical Connectivity

indicators.name: People using at least basic drinking water services (% of population)
indicators.description: The percentage of people using at least basic water services.  This indicator encompasses both people using basic water services as well as those using safely managed water services.  Basic drinking water services is defined as drinking water from an improved source, provided collection time is not more than 30 minutes for a round trip.  Improved water sources include piped water, boreholes or tubewells, protected dug wells, protected springs, and packaged or delivered water.
indicators.inform_group: Lack of Coping Capacity > Infrastructure > Physical Connectivity

indicators.name: Road density
indicators.description: Road density is the ratio of the length of the country's total road network to the country's land area. The road network includes all roads in the country: motorways, highways, main or national roads, secondary or regional roads, and other urban and rural roads.
indicators.inform_group: Lack of Coping Capacity > Infrastructure > Physical Connectivity

indicators.name: Current health expenditure per capita
indicators.description: Current expenditures on health per capita expressed in international dollars at purchasing power parity (PPP).
indicators.inform_group: Lack of Coping Capacity > Infrastructure > Access to health care

indicators.name: Physicians density
indicators.description: Number of medical doctors (physicians), including generalist and specialist medical practitioners, per 10,000 population.
indicators.inform_group: Lack of Coping Capacity > Infrastructure > Access to health care

indicators.name: Maternal Mortality Ratio
indicators.description: Maternal death is the death of a woman while pregnant or within 42 days of termination of pregnancy, irrespective of the duration and site of the pregnancy, from any cause related to or aggravated by the pregnancy or its management but not from accidental or incidental causes. The Maternal Mortality Ratio is defined by the number of maternal deaths per 100,000 live births.
indicators.inform_group: Lack of Coping Capacity > Infrastructure > Access to health care

indicators.name: Population affected by natural disasters in the last 3 years
indicators.description: To account for increased vulnerability during the recovery period after a disaster, people affected by recent shocks in the past 3 years are considered. The affected people from the most recent year are considered fully while affected people from the previous years are scaled down with the factor 0.5 and 0.25 for the second and third year, respectively, assuming that recovery decreases vulnerability progressively.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Vulnerable Groups > Other Vulnerable Groups > Recent shocks

indicators.name: Refugees and asylum-seekers by country of asylum
indicators.description: “Persons of concern” includes refugees, asylum-seekers, returnees, stateless persons and groups of internally displaced persons (IDPs).
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Vulnerable Groups > Uprooted people

indicators.name: Internally displaced persons (IDPs)
indicators.description: “Persons of concern” includes refugees, asylum-seekers, returnees, stateless persons and groups of internally displaced persons (IDPs).
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Vulnerable Groups > Uprooted people

indicators.name: Returned refugees
indicators.description: “Persons of concern” includes refugees, asylum-seekers, returnees, stateless persons and groups of internally displaced persons (IDPs).
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Vulnerable Groups > Uprooted people

indicators.name: Child Mortality
indicators.description: This indicator shows the probability of death between birth and the end of the fifth year per 1000 live births.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Vulnerable Groups > Other Vulnerable Groups > Health of children under 5

indicators.name: Children Under Weight
indicators.description: This indicator shows the ratio between weight and age of children under five.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Vulnerable Groups > Other Vulnerable Groups > Health of children under 5

indicators.name: Average dietary supply adequacy
indicators.description: Average dietary energy supply as a percentage of the average dietary energy requirement.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Vulnerable Groups > Other Vulnerable Groups > Food Security - Food Availability

indicators.name: Prevalence of undernourishment
indicators.description: The Prevalence of Undernourishment expresses the probability that a randomly selected individual from the population consumes an amount of calories that is insufficient to cover her/his energy requirement for an active and healthy life.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Vulnerable Groups > Other Vulnerable Groups > Food Security - Food Utilization

indicators.name: Total population
indicators.description: Estimates (up to 2021) and medium projections from 2022.
indicators.inform_group: Common

indicators.name: GHSL multi-temporal Population Grid
indicators.description: The GHS-POP spatial raster product (GHS-POP_GLOBE_R2023) depicts the distribution of human population, expressed as the number of people per cell. Residential population estimates at 5 years interval between 1975 and 2030.
indicators.inform_group: Hazards & Exposure calculations

indicators.name: Population density (people per sq. km of land area)
indicators.description: Population density is midyear population divided by land area in square kilo meters.
indicators.inform_group: Hazards & Exposure > Natural > Epidemic > P2P / Water and Food borne

indicators.name: INFORM Natural hazard & exposure category
indicators.description: Aggregated score of the natural hazard & exposure category (shared by all natural hazards).

indicators.name: INFORM Vulnerability (dimension index)
indicators.description: Aggregated index of the Vulnerability dimension.

indicators.name: INFORM Lack of Coping Capacity (dimension index)
indicators.description: Aggregated index of the Lack of Coping Capacity dimension.

indicators.name: INFORM Risk Index (overall)
indicators.description: Overall INFORM Risk index (geometric mean of the three dimensions).

indicators.name: Income Gini coefficient - Inequality in income or consumption

indicators.name: Humanitarian aid per capita
indicators.description: The Financial Tracking Service (FTS) is a centralized source of curated, continuously updated data and information on humanitarian funding flows, where government donors, UN-administered funds, UN agencies, NGOs and other humanitarian actors exchange data and information. The indicator is expressed as the three-year rolling sum of total humanitarian assistance received divided by population (USD per capita), with the three-year aggregation used to smooth single-year emergency spikes and better reflect the structural humanitarian funding base of a country.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economical Dependency

indicators.name: Humanitarian aid per capita instability
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in humanitarian aid funding caused by external shocks and donor behaviour. Unstable humanitarian funding has a large effect on the planning and delivery of emergency response and increases the risk of unmet needs in crisis-affected populations. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the value of annual humanitarian aid per capita and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of humanitarian aid per capita) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Development aid per capita
indicators.description: Net Official Development Assistance (ODA) consists of disbursements of concessional loans and grants by official agencies of the Development Assistance Committee (DAC), multilateral institutions, and non-DAC countries to promote economic development and welfare in ODA recipient countries. The indicator is expressed as the two-year lagged sum of annual net ODA received divided by population (USD per capita), with the two-year aggregation accounting for disbursement lags between aid commitments and actual delivery.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Development aid per capita instability
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in the absolute volume of official development assistance per person caused by external shocks and changes in donor allocations. Unstable per capita ODA has a large effect on the availability of resources for basic services and infrastructure investment and increases the risk of development reversals in fragile and aid-dependent states. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the annual value of net ODA received per capita and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of ODA per capita) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Net ODA received (% of GNI)
indicators.description: Net Official Development Assistance (ODA) consists of disbursements of loans made on concessional terms (net of repayments of principal) and grants by official agencies of the members of the Development Assistance Committee (DAC), by multilateral institutions, and by non-DAC countries to promote economic development and welfare in countries and territories in the DAC list of ODA recipients. It includes loans with a grant element of at least 25 percent (calculated at a rate of discount of 10 percent).
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Net ODA received instability (% of GNI)
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in official development assistance relative to its national income caused by external shocks and changes in donor priorities. Unstable ODA as a share of GNI has a large effect on public revenues and long-term development planning and increases fiscal risk for aid-dependent economies. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the annual value of net ODA received as a percentage of GNI and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of ODA % GNI) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Volume of remittances as a proportion of total GDP (%)

indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Volume of remittances as a proportion of total GDP instability (%)
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in personal remittances relative to its economy caused by external shocks including economic downturns in host countries, exchange rate movements, and changes in migration policy. Unstable remittance inflows have a large effect on household income, private consumption, and poverty levels and increase the vulnerability of remittance-dependent populations to sudden income loss. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the annual value of personal remittances received as a percentage of GDP and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of remittances % GDP) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.

indicators.name: Improved water source
indicators.description:
The indicator defines the percentage of population with reasonable access (within one km) to an adequate amount of water (20 litres per person) through a household connection, public standpipe well or spring, or rain water system.

indicators.name: People using at least basic sanitation services (% of population)

indicators.name: People using at least basic drinking water services (% of population)

indicators.description: The Gender Inequality Index (GII) reflects gender-based disadvantages in three dimensions—reproductive health, empowerment and the labour market. The value of GII range between 0 to 1, with 0 being 0% inequality, indicating women fare equally in comparison to men and 1 being 100% inequality, indicating women fare poorly in comparison to men.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Inequality

indicators.name: Income Gini coefficient - Inequality in income or consumption
indicators.description: Gini index measures the extent to which the distribution of income or consumption expenditure among individuals or households within an economy deviates from a perfectly equal distribution. Thus a Gini index of 0 represents perfect equality, while an index of 100 implies perfect inequality.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Inequality

indicators.name: Humanitarian aid per capita
indicators.description: The Financial Tracking Service (FTS) is a centralized source of curated, continuously updated data and information on humanitarian funding flows, where government donors, UN-administered funds, UN agencies, NGOs and other humanitarian actors exchange data and information. The indicator is expressed as the three-year rolling sum of total humanitarian assistance received divided by population (USD per capita), with the three-year aggregation used to smooth single-year emergency spikes and better reflect the structural humanitarian funding base of a country.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economical Dependency

indicators.name: Humanitarian aid per capita instability
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in humanitarian aid funding caused by external shocks and donor behaviour. Unstable humanitarian funding has a large effect on the planning and delivery of emergency response and increases the risk of unmet needs in crisis-affected populations. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the value of annual humanitarian aid per capita and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of humanitarian aid per capita) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Development aid per capita
indicators.description: Net Official Development Assistance (ODA) consists of disbursements of concessional loans and grants by official agencies of the Development Assistance Committee (DAC), multilateral institutions, and non-DAC countries to promote economic development and welfare in ODA recipient countries. The indicator is expressed as the two-year lagged sum of annual net ODA received divided by population (USD per capita), with the two-year aggregation accounting for disbursement lags between aid commitments and actual delivery.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Development aid per capita instability
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in the absolute volume of official development assistance per person caused by external shocks and changes in donor allocations. Unstable per capita ODA has a large effect on the availability of resources for basic services and infrastructure investment and increases the risk of development reversals in fragile and aid-dependent states. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the annual value of net ODA received per capita and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of ODA per capita) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Net ODA received (% of GNI)
indicators.description: Net Official Development Assistance (ODA) consists of disbursements of loans made on concessional terms (net of repayments of principal) and grants by official agencies of the members of the Development Assistance Committee (DAC), by multilateral institutions, and by non-DAC countries to promote economic development and welfare in countries and territories in the DAC list of ODA recipients. It includes loans with a grant element of at least 25 percent (calculated at a rate of discount of 10 percent).
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Net ODA received instability (% of GNI)
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in official development assistance relative to its national income caused by external shocks and changes in donor priorities. Unstable ODA as a share of GNI has a large effect on public revenues and long-term development planning and increases fiscal risk for aid-dependent economies. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the annual value of net ODA received as a percentage of GNI and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of ODA % GNI) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Volume of remittances as a proportion of total GDP (%)
indicators.description: Personal remittances received as proportion of GDP is the inflow of personal remittances expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Volume of remittances as a proportion of total GDP instability (%)
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in personal remittances relative to its economy caused by external shocks including economic downturns in host countries, exchange rate movements, and changes in migration policy. Unstable remittance inflows have a large effect on household income, private consumption, and poverty levels and increase the vulnerability of remittance-dependent populations to sudden income loss. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the annual value of personal remittances received as a percentage of GDP and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of remittances % GDP) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Income Gini coefficient - Inequality in income or consumption
indicators.description: Gini index measures the extent to which the distribution of income or consumption expenditure among individuals or households within an economy deviates from a perfectly equal distribution. indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Inequality

indicators.name: Humanitarian aid per capita
indicators.description: The Financial Tracking Service (FTS) is a centralized source of curated, continuously updated data and information on humanitarian funding flows, where government donors, UN-administered funds, UN agencies, NGOs and other humanitarian actors exchange data and information. The indicator is expressed as the three-year rolling sum of total humanitarian assistance received divided by population (USD per capita), with the three-year aggregation used to smooth single-year emergency spikes and better reflect the structural humanitarian funding base of a country.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economical Dependency

indicators.name: Humanitarian aid per capita instability
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in humanitarian aid funding caused by external shocks and donor behaviour. Unstable humanitarian funding has a large effect on the planning and delivery of emergency response and increases the risk of unmet needs in crisis-affected populations. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the value of annual humanitarian aid per capita and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of humanitarian aid per capita) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Development aid per capita
indicators.description: Net Official Development Assistance (ODA) consists of disbursements of concessional loans and grants by official agencies of the Development Assistance Committee (DAC), multilateral institutions, and non-DAC countries to promote economic development and welfare in ODA recipient countries. The indicator is expressed as the two-year lagged sum of annual net ODA received divided by population (USD per capita), with the two-year aggregation accounting for disbursement lags between aid commitments and actual delivery.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Development aid per capita instability
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in the absolute volume of official development assistance per person caused by external shocks and changes in donor allocations. Unstable per capita ODA has a large effect on the availability of resources for basic services and infrastructure investment and increases the risk of development reversals in fragile and aid-dependent states. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the annual value of net ODA received per capita and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of ODA per capita) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Net ODA received (% of GNI)
indicators.description: Net Official Development Assistance (ODA) consists of disbursements of loans made on concessional terms (net of repayments of principal) and grants by official agencies of the members of the Development Assistance Committee (DAC), by multilateral institutions, and by non-DAC countries to promote economic development and welfare in countries and territories in the DAC list of ODA recipients. It includes loans with a grant element of at least 25 percent (calculated at a rate of discount of 10 percent).
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Net ODA received instability (% of GNI)

The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of ODA % GNI) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Volume of remittances as a proportion of total GDP instability (%)

indicators.description: The Gender Inequality Index (GII) reflects gender-based disadvantages in three dimensions—reproductive health, empowerment and the labour market. The value of GII range between 0 to 1, with 0 being 0% inequality, indicating women fare equally in comparison to men and 1 being 100% inequality, indicating women fare poorly in comparison to men.

indicators.name: Income Gini coefficient - Inequality in income or consumption
indicators.description: Gini index measures the extent to which the distribution of income or consumption expenditure among individuals or households within an economy deviates from a perfectly equal distribution. Thus a Gini index of 0 represents perfect equality, while an index of 100 implies perfect inequality.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Inequality

indicators.name: Humanitarian aid per capita
indicators.description: The Financial Tracking Service (FTS) is a centralized source of curated, continuously updated data and information on humanitarian funding flows, where government donors, UN-administered funds, UN agencies, NGOs and other humanitarian actors exchange data and information. The indicator is expressed as the three-year rolling sum of total humanitarian assistance received divided by population (USD per capita), with the three-year aggregation used to smooth single-year emergency spikes and better reflect the structural humanitarian funding base of a country.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economical Dependency

indicators.name: Humanitarian aid per capita instability
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in humanitarian aid funding caused by external shocks and donor behaviour. Unstable humanitarian funding has a large effect on the planning and delivery of emergency response and increases the risk of unmet needs in crisis-affected populations. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the value of annual humanitarian aid per capita and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of humanitarian aid per capita) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Development aid per capita
indicators.description: Net Official Development Assistance (ODA) consists of disbursements of concessional loans and grants by official agencies of the Development Assistance Committee (DAC), multilateral institutions, and non-DAC countries to promote economic development and welfare in ODA recipient countries. The indicator is expressed as the two-year lagged sum of annual net ODA received divided by population (USD per capita), with the two-year aggregation accounting for disbursement lags between aid commitments and actual delivery.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Development aid per capita instability
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in the absolute volume of official development assistance per person caused by external shocks and changes in donor allocations. Unstable per capita ODA has a large effect on the availability of resources for basic services and infrastructure investment and increases the risk of development reversals in fragile and aid-dependent states. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the annual value of net ODA received per capita and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of ODA per capita) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Net ODA received (% of GNI)
indicators.description: Net Official Development Assistance (ODA) consists of disbursements of loans made on concessional terms (net of repayments of principal) and grants by official agencies of the members of the Development Assistance Committee (DAC), by multilateral institutions, and by non-DAC countries to promote economic development and welfare in countries and territories in the DAC list of ODA recipients. It includes loans with a grant element of at least 25 percent (calculated at a rate of discount of 10 percent).
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Net ODA received instability (% of GNI)
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in official development assistance relative to its national income caused by external shocks and changes in donor priorities. Unstable ODA as a share of GNI has a large effect on public revenues and long-term development planning and increases fiscal risk for aid-dependent economies. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the annual value of net ODA received as a percentage of GNI and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of ODA % GNI) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Volume of remittances as a proportion of total GDP (%)
indicators.description: Personal remittances received as proportion of GDP is the inflow of personal remittances expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Volume of remittances as a proportion of total GDP instability (%)
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in personal remittances relative to its economy caused by external shocks including economic downturns in host countries, exchange rate movements, and changes in migration policy. Unstable remittance inflows have a large effect on household income, private consumption, and poverty levels and increase the vulnerability of remittance-dependent populations to sudden income loss. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the annual value of personal remittances received as a percentage of GDP and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of remittances % GDP) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Income Gini coefficient - Inequality in income or consumption

indicators.name: Humanitarian aid per capita
indicators.description: The Financial Tracking Service (FTS) is a centralized source of curated, continuously updated data and information on humanitarian funding flows, where government donors, UN-administered funds, UN agencies, NGOs and other humanitarian actors exchange data and information. The indicator is expressed as the three-year rolling sum of total humanitarian assistance received divided by population (USD per capita), with the three-year aggregation used to smooth single-year emergency spikes and better reflect the structural humanitarian funding base of a country.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economical Dependency

indicators.name: Humanitarian aid per capita instability
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in humanitarian aid funding caused by external shocks and donor behaviour. Unstable humanitarian funding has a large effect on the planning and delivery of emergency response and increases the risk of unmet needs in crisis-affected populations. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the value of annual humanitarian aid per capita and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of humanitarian aid per capita) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Development aid per capita
indicators.description: Net Official Development Assistance (ODA) consists of disbursements of concessional loans and grants by official agencies of the Development Assistance Committee (DAC), multilateral institutions, and non-DAC countries to promote economic development and welfare in ODA recipient countries. The indicator is expressed as the two-year lagged sum of annual net ODA received divided by population (USD per capita), with the two-year aggregation accounting for disbursement lags between aid commitments and actual delivery.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Development aid per capita instability
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in the absolute volume of official development assistance per person caused by external shocks and changes in donor allocations. Unstable per capita ODA has a large effect on the availability of resources for basic services and infrastructure investment and increases the risk of development reversals in fragile and aid-dependent states. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the annual value of net ODA received per capita and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of ODA per capita) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Net ODA received (% of GNI)
indicators.description: Net Official Development Assistance (ODA) consists of disbursements of loans made on concessional terms (net of repayments of principal) and grants by official agencies of the members of the Development Assistance Committee (DAC), by multilateral institutions, and by non-DAC countries to promote economic development and welfare in countries and territories in the DAC list of ODA recipients. It includes loans with a grant element of at least 25 percent (calculated at a rate of discount of 10 percent).
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Net ODA received instability (% of GNI)
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in official development assistance relative to its national income caused by external shocks and changes in donor priorities. Unstable ODA as a share of GNI has a large effect on public revenues and long-term development planning and increases fiscal risk for aid-dependent economies. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the annual value of net ODA received as a percentage of GNI and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of ODA % GNI) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Volume of remittances as a proportion of total GDP (%)
indicators.description: Personal remittances received as proportion of GDP is the inflow of personal remittances expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Volume of remittances as a proportion of total GDP instability (%)
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in personal remittances relative to its economy caused by external shocks including economic downturns in host countries, exchange rate movements, and changes in migration policy. Unstable remittance inflows have a large effect on household income, private consumption, and poverty levels and increase the vulnerability of remittance-dependent populations to sudden income loss. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the annual value of personal remittances received as a percentage of GDP and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of remittances % GDP) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.

indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in personal remittances relative to its economy caused by external shocks including economic downturns in host countries, exchange rate movements, and changes in migration policy. Unstable remittance inflows have a large effect on household income, private consumption, and poverty levels and increase the vulnerability of remittance-dependent populations to sudden income loss. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the annual value of personal remittances received as a percentage of GDP and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of remittances % GDP) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.

indicators.name: Access to electricity

indicators.name: Internet Users

indicators.name: Mobile celluar subscriptions
indicators.description: Mobile cellular telephone subscriptions are subscriptions to a public mobile telephone service using cellular technology, which provide access to the public switched telephone network. Post-paid and prepaid subscriptions are included.

indicators.name: Improved sanitation facilities
indicators.description: Access to improved sanitation facilities refers to the percentage of the population using improved sanitation facilities. indicators.inform_group: Lack of Coping Capacity > Infrastructure > Physical Connectivity

indicators.name: Improved water source
indicators.description:
The indicator defines the percentage of population with reasonable access (within one km) to an adequate amount of water (20 litres per person) through a household connection, public standpipe well or spring, or rain water system.
An improved drinking-water source is defined as one that, by nature of its construction or through active intervention, is protected from outside contamination, in particular from contamination with faecal matter.
indicators.inform_group: Lack of Coping Capacity > Infrastructure > Physical Connectivity

indicators.name: People using at least basic sanitation services (% of population)

This indicator encompasses both people using basic sanitation services as well as those using safely managed sanitation services.   Improved sanitation facilities include flush/pour flush to piped sewer systems, septic tanks or pit latrines; ventilated improved pit latrines, compositing toilets or pit latrines with slabs.
indicators.inform_group: Lack of Coping Capacity > Infrastructure > Physical Connectivity

indicators.name: People using at least basic drinking water services (% of population)

indicators.inform_group: Lack of Coping Capacity > Infrastructure > Physical Connectivity

indicators.name: Road density

indicators.name: Multidimensional Poverty Index
indicators.description: The Multidimensional Poverty (MPI) Index identifies overlapping deprivations at the household level across the same three dimensions as the Human Development Index (living standards, health, and education) and shows the average number of poor people and deprivations with which poor households contend.

indicators.name: Gender Inequality Index
indicators.description: The Gender Inequality Index (GII) reflects gender-based disadvantages in three dimensions—reproductive health, empowerment and the labour market. The value of GII range between 0 to 1, with 0 being 0% inequality, indicating women fare equally in comparison to men and 1 being 100% inequality, indicating women fare poorly in comparison to men.

indicators.name: Income Gini coefficient - Inequality in income or consumption
indicators.description: Gini index measures the extent to which the distribution of income or consumption expenditure among individuals or households within an economy deviates from a perfectly equal distribution. Thus a Gini index of 0 represents perfect equality, while an index of 100 implies perfect inequality.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Inequality

indicators.name: Humanitarian aid per capita
indicators.description: The Financial Tracking Service (FTS) is a centralized source of curated, continuously updated data and information on humanitarian funding flows, where government donors, UN-administered funds, UN agencies, NGOs and other humanitarian actors exchange data and information. The indicator is expressed as the three-year rolling sum of total humanitarian assistance received divided by population (USD per capita), with the three-year aggregation used to smooth single-year emergency spikes and better reflect the structural humanitarian funding base of a country.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economical Dependency

indicators.name: Humanitarian aid per capita instability
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in humanitarian aid funding caused by external shocks and donor behaviour. Unstable humanitarian funding has a large effect on the planning and delivery of emergency response and increases the risk of unmet needs in crisis-affected populations. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the value of annual humanitarian aid per capita and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of humanitarian aid per capita) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Development aid per capita
indicators.description: Net Official Development Assistance (ODA) consists of disbursements of concessional loans and grants by official agencies of the Development Assistance Committee (DAC), multilateral institutions, and non-DAC countries to promote economic development and welfare in ODA recipient countries. The indicator is expressed as the two-year lagged sum of annual net ODA received divided by population (USD per capita), with the two-year aggregation accounting for disbursement lags between aid commitments and actual delivery.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Development aid per capita instability
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in the absolute volume of official development assistance per person caused by external shocks and changes in donor allocations. Unstable per capita ODA has a large effect on the availability of resources for basic services and infrastructure investment and increases the risk of development reversals in fragile and aid-dependent states. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the annual value of net ODA received per capita and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of ODA per capita) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Net ODA received (% of GNI)
indicators.description: Net Official Development Assistance (ODA) consists of disbursements of loans made on concessional terms (net of repayments of principal) and grants by official agencies of the members of the Development Assistance Committee (DAC), by multilateral institutions, and by non-DAC countries to promote economic development and welfare in countries and territories in the DAC list of ODA recipients. It includes loans with a grant element of at least 25 percent (calculated at a rate of discount of 10 percent).
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency

indicators.name: Net ODA received instability (% of GNI)
indicators.description: The indicator measures a country's vulnerability to fluctuations in official development assistance relative to its national income caused by external shocks and changes in donor priorities. Unstable ODA as a share of GNI has a large effect on public revenues and long-term development planning and increases fiscal risk for aid-dependent economies. The indicator is measured as the standard deviation of the difference between the annual value of net ODA received as a percentage of GNI and its 7-year trend. The estimated trend is mixed and includes both stochastic (a one-year lagged value of ODA % GNI) and quadratic deterministic (a time variable and its square) components.
indicators.inform_group: Vulnerability > Social-Economics Vulnerability > Economic Dependency
